newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl to meet leader of coal miners' union.
newsitem.headline: Kohl to meet leader of coal miners' union.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl will meet Hans Berger, head of the IG Bergbau coal miners' union, on March 6 to discuss future government subsidies of domestic coal mining, IG Bergbau said on Wednesday.
Government spokesman Peter Hausmann confirmed that the meeting was scheduled.
Bonn, under pressure to slash spending and reduce government deficits, aims to cut the subsidies, which now total about 10 billion marks ($6 billion) a year.
IG Bergbau has said the industry could survive with 6.5 billion to seven billion marks a year in government help, but only by halving the number of miners to about 50,000.
Kohl has called that proposal unrealistic.
About 100,000 miners and their supporters marched in the Ruhr Valley mining region earlier this month to call for continued subsidies.
German hard coal, which must be dug from deep beneath the earth, costs several times as much as imports, but Bonn has seen fit to maintain at least a token domestic industry.
Berger told reporters he did not expect the March 6 meeting to product a final decision, but that the situation must be clarified by Easter.
Kohl hopes to mount talks with representatives of Germany's main coal-mining states Saarland and North Rhine-Westphalia as well as mining companies, but no date has been set.
He discussed the coal issue with Social Democrat leader Oskar Lafontaine, who is also premier of Saarland, on Monday after their "tax summit".
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.671 German Marks)
